newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bonds flat amid stepped-up retail bid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bonds flat amid stepped-up retail bid.

text.p: An improved retail bid for U.S. corporate bonds marked an otherwise quiet session, dealers said, while new issuance commanded market attention.

The high-grade primary market featured $300 million in 10-year A1/A-plus rated notes from WMX Technologies, priced to yield 7.04 percent, or 54 basis points over the when-issued 10-year Treasury. The deal was increased in size by $100 million to meet investor demand, according to syndicate sources.
Secondary prices were little changed and spreads were held firm against U.S. Treasuries, traders said.

Brisk retail bidding into mid-session busied trading desks, players said, although it failed to pressure spreads. Expectations of heavy new issuance were waning, meanwhile, buttressing the bid for high-grade paper.
"I think everybody thought we'd have (heavy issuance) by now and we haven't seen it yet," one trader said. "Everybody feels somewhat comfortable with it now."

New issues were trading unchanged from Monday's close, traders said. Smith Barney Holdings' $200 million 7.125 percent 10-year notes were seen trading at the original issue spread of 68 basis points over the Treasury curve.
In high-yield trade, prices were mostly unchanged in thin trade, dealers said. But some losers of Monday continued their drift down, including Penn Traffic's 10.25 percent debt of 2002.
The notes lost one point on Monday to 89 bid.

High-yield desks were focused on some new issues set to price on Tuesday, including $225 million in B2/single-B senior subordinated notes of 2006 from Goss Graphic Systems via CS First Boston Corp, $350 million in 144A senior subordinated notes of 2008 from Paging Network Inc via Goldman Sachs & Co and $150 million 10-year notes from Outdoor Systems via CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp.

U.S. Treasuries were mostly static at midday, losing marginal gains achieved after the Richmond Federal Reserve manufacturing shipments index fell to 2 in September from 16 in August. The revenues index fell to negative 2 from 21.
Also supporting fixed-income markets was a 0.1 percent drop in the BTM/Scroders index in the week ended October 5 following a 1.2 percent drop in the prior week, analysts said.
The market will contend with the auction of $10.0 billion 10-year U.S. Treasury notes on Tuesday afternoon.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was quoted up 2/32 at 99-18/32 to yield 6.78 percent at 1230 EDT/1630 GMT.
